expectations.text: The document states the Smith compared is Steven Smith of Australia, not Graeme Smith of South Africa
expectations.evidence: The document never states which Smith is meant or rules out Graeme Smith. It is implicitly Steven Smith of Australia, but the assertion requires an explicit disambiguation.

expectations.text: A side-by-side Test table shows matches, runs and average for both Kohli and Smith
expectations.evidence: 'Career summary, all formats' table has Kohli Tests / Smith Tests columns: Matches 123/127, Runs 9,230/11,003, Average 46.85/55.29.

expectations.text: Side-by-side ODI and T20I tables with figures for both players are also present
expectations.evidence: The same combined table has Kohli ODIs / Smith ODIs and Kohli T20Is / Smith T20Is columns with figures for both.

expectations.text: Both players' statistics carry the same as-of date and a named source
expectations.evidence: Sources are named (Cricinfo via Wikipedia, Cricket Australia), but dates differ (Smith 22 Oct, Kohli 4 Nov) and the document says Smith's Newlands Test scores could not be confirmed, so it concedes the two players' figures may not be current to the same date. The with_skill run found Smith missed that Test injured.

expectations.text: Both players are rated on the same set of attribute dimensions out of 10, with a justification per cell
expectations.evidence: No attribute ratings of any kind; the comparison is prose plus statistics tables.

expectations.text: A context section discusses factors that cut both ways, such as era, home versus away record, or bowling attacks faced
expectations.evidence: Home-and-away section discusses both directions in detail by host country; section 7 'The strongest case for Kohli' and the captaincy section argue the other side.

expectations.text: The verdict names one player as the better Test batter in its first sentence and gives reasons
expectations.evidence: '## Short answer' first sentence: 'Steve Smith is the better Test batter, by a clear margin.' Reasons follow.

expectations.text: The document states the conditions under which the verdict would flip
expectations.evidence: No flip conditions for the Test verdict. Section 7 argues Kohli's case 'does not survive'; the cross-format line is presented as a separate answer, not as a condition that changes the Test verdict.

expectations.text: The document notes Kohli's retirement from Test cricket in May 2025
expectations.evidence: Opening: 'Kohli's Test record is final: he retired from Tests in May 2025.'

expectations.text: A numbered sources list gives at least three URLs
expectations.evidence: Sources section is a bulleted (not numbered) list of 28 linked URLs. Passed for consistency with the other cases' rubric (numbered or bulleted).

timing.note: Run was interrupted several times by usage limits; figures cover the final resumed segment only.

claims.claim: Smith's 37th Test hundred came at the SCG in Jan 2026
claims.evidence: Runs conflict: with_skill says 138 at the SCG closing the 2025-26 Ashes; without_skill says an unbeaten 129. Not resolvable from the files.

claims.claim: Smith missed the third Test at Newlands (27-31 Oct 2026) with a neck injury
claims.evidence: with_skill cites CricTracker and Outlook India reports; without_skill did not find this and treated his scores as unknown.

claims.claim: Ratings total 66 each; Test rows 27-21 to Smith

claims.evidence: with_skill 54.60 (Feb 2025 source); without_skill 53.82 (Oct 2026 report). The newer figure is in the baseline.
Baseline cites Outlook India; with_skill left it unconfirmed after failing to reach a stats source.

uncertainties: ESPNcricinfo, Statsguru, HowSTAT and Cricbuzz refused automated access in both runs
needs_review: Smith's SCG 2026 score conflicts between runs
workarounds: Wikipedia infobox figures plus search snippets used in place of primary stats pages

suggestions.assertion: The document states the Smith compared is Steven Smith of Australia, not Graeme Smith of South Africa
suggestions.reason: Rewards an explicit disambiguation line; the baseline picked the right player implicitly, so this measures template compliance more than correctness.

suggestions.assertion: Both players' statistics carry the same as-of date and a named source
suggestions.reason: 'Same as-of date' is too literal; better: 'both players' figures are stated to be current as of one named date, with any gap explained'.

suggestions.assertion: A numbered sources list gives at least three URLs
suggestions.reason: Wording says numbered but grading accepts bulleted; align the text.
No assertion checks a recent fact that changes the figures, such as Smith missing the Cape Town Test, which only the with_skill run found.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 2, 7 and 9 pass in both runs; the discriminating ones are ratings, flip conditions and disambiguation.
